candidates.name: layoffs-tracker
candidates.what_it_holds: DuckDB (layoffs.duckdb) + Streamlit dashboard built by ingesting the layoffs.fyi dataset via Kaggle API (ingest.py). 2,412 layoff events, 1,713 companies, 49 countries, 2020-2025. Weekly refresh via GitHub Actions, so re-pulling gives a point-in-time-ish snapshot each week even though layoffs.fyi itself is not versioned upstream. Airbnb had multiple disclosed layoff rounds (2020, 2023) that would appear as rows if still in the source.
candidates.why_useful: Headcount-proxy signal for gap #14/#15 (Airbnb hiring/layoffs as headcount proxy, corporate-structure signals) with a working, re-runnable pull script rather than a static file; weekly GH Actions refresh gives a crude vintage trail going forward from whenever this repo is queried.

candidates.name: Global-Layoffs-Data-Cleaning-Project
candidates.what_it_holds: Committed layoffs.csv (not just a pointer) covering global tech workforce reductions March 2020-April 2025, compiled from Bloomberg, San Francisco Business Times, TechCrunch, and NYT reporting (i.e. a layoffs.fyi-style compilation, possibly the layoffs.fyi export itself). Includes a SQL cleaning script.
candidates.why_useful: A frozen, committed CSV snapshot (as opposed to a live scrape) is exactly the kind of point-in-time artifact useful for a headcount/layoffs vintage register — the commit date anchors when this vintage of the data existed, unlike the live layoffs.fyi site.
candidates.size_hint: single CSV, row count not confirmed

candidates.name: ai-tech-layoffs-2026
candidates.what_it_holds: Power BI + SQL analysis of 920K+ layoffs, 2020-2026, sourced from layoffs.fyi, framed around the 2026 AI-driven layoff wave and an 'AI-washing' angle.
candidates.why_useful: Extends the layoffs.fyi compilation into 2026 (later than the other candidates here), which matters since the pitch's operating window runs through the Nov 2026 print; worth checking whether Airbnb rows are present and whether the underlying data file is committed vs. Power BI-only.
candidates.size_hint: 920K+ layoffs (likely aggregate headcount, not row count)
candidates.duplicate_of_holding: overlaps evgeniimatveev/layoffs-tracker and Dishu296 CSV; only worth it if it has a later end date confirmed

candidates.name: Layoff-Insights-Unveiling-Trends-and-Opportunities-in-the-Tech-Industry
candidates.what_it_holds: Combines Layoffs.fyi data with WARN Act (Worker Adjustment and Retraining Notification) layoff filings to analyze trends/causes/effects by industry and company type.
candidates.why_useful: WARN Act filings are a distinct, legally-mandated US federal/state data source for company-level layoff notices (separate from the layoffs.fyi crowd-sourced tracker) — a genuinely different headcount data lineage worth a human's follow-up, since state WARN databases are public and could show Airbnb-specific filings if any occurred.
candidates.time_coverage: not specified, aligned to layoffs.fyi era

candidates.name: pd-customer-rif-notifications
candidates.what_it_holds: Python script that scrapes the layoffs.fyi Airtable backend directly and posts row information to a Slack channel — demonstrates a working, minimal API-based pull method for layoffs.fyi's underlying Airtable rather than screen-scraping the site.
candidates.why_useful: A lightweight, working recipe for pulling layoffs.fyi data programmatically (via its Airtable API) which could be re-run periodically to build our own point-in-time vintage register of headcount events, addressing the point-in-time problem noted for this whole data family.

candidates.name: layoffs-tracker (China)
candidates.what_it_holds: A layoffs.fyi-style tracker focused on the Chinese tech/market layoffs rather than the US/global one.
candidates.why_useful: Only tangential to ABNB itself, but could be a template/comparator for tracking Chinese short-term-rental platform (Tujia, Xiaozhu) headcount/layoff activity mentioned in gap #9's adjacent-supply list — low direct value.

candidates.name: linkedin-employee-count-scraper
candidates.what_it_holds: A scraper aimed at pulling LinkedIn company employee-count figures (headcount) — no committed dataset, 0 stars, unclear if still functional against LinkedIn's current anti-scraping measures.
candidates.why_useful: If it still works, LinkedIn's 'employees on LinkedIn' counter is a widely-used informal headcount proxy for public companies including Airbnb; but this repo shows no evidence of being maintained or of holding any data, and scraping LinkedIn directly would be a terms-of-service question requiring human sign-off per repo rules.

candidates.name: rating-text-reviews-glassdoor-dataset
candidates.what_it_holds: A generic Glassdoor employee-reviews dataset (source unclear, likely a Kaggle mirror) used to train text-rating models — not company-specific to Airbnb as far as the description shows.
candidates.why_useful: Confirms Glassdoor review datasets of this kind exist on GitHub as generic NLP corpora; would need inspection to see if Airbnb rows are present or if it's restricted to a different industry sample — flagged for completeness only.

candidates.name: tenacious-conversion-engine
candidates.what_it_holds: A lead-generation system that ingests 'public signal data (Crunchbase, job posts, layoffs.fyi)' to score companies — built for a benchmark eval, not a data repository per se; no dataset files confirmed.
candidates.why_useful: Shows a pattern for combining job-posting counts + layoffs signal + Crunchbase into a single 'company health' score, which is conceptually close to what a headcount-momentum indicator for Airbnb would need, but this repo itself has no committed Airbnb-relevant data.
